verdict.english_script:
I only very recently got out of unemployment, so I'm going to give you a little tip so you can get out of it too.
Look, I worked at the same company for 5 years, so when I left I was still using my Canva CVs, these ones you see here.
The thing is, AI has come a long way, and big multinationals now use ATS systems to filter the huge number of CVs they get.
I have a friend in HR, and she recommended an app to tailor my CV so it gets through the ATS filters, so that at least a person reads my CV instead of a machine rejecting me straight away.
So I'm going to share it with you.
You go to this site called jobstep.io, and it analyzes your whole CV. The first time I did it, mine came out terrible, 38%, so let's improve it.
I bring you solutions to the problem.
We click the AI editor and it improves it for us. It got mine up to 96, and look how gorgeous this CV is, come on.

verdict.english_script:
10 job offers?
10 job offers is what I got in the last week!
So I just opened my email, which I hadn't checked for like 5 days, and I saw this.
I'm in shock.
Do you see this? Look, look, look.
I'm so happy I feel sick.
And you know what my biggest mistake was?
I thought it didn't matter what your CV looks like or how it's written.
I was like: eh, if it says what they need, and if they need you, they'll hire you.
Well, now that I've changed my CV, I got 10 job offers, and I can't believe that mistake kept me unemployed for 6 months.
I'm not going to gatekeep, because it really helped me.
So, I found this site on TikTok, jobstep.io, and I uploaded my old CV there so it could rate it, and it was a disaster.
Like, nothing about it was good.
The app literally guides you through the steps you need to take to make your CV better.
So the AI literally asks you about yourself, about the job, what you do, what your field is, and so on.
And it completely changes the format, so it's really professional, worded the right way, and gets through all the filters it needs to so it reaches HR.
At the end, of course, you can change the color and choose the layout.
It doesn't matter what you like, it makes no difference.
What matters is that the format is right.
So there you go, now you know: if you have the same problem, don't waste time like I did.
So if anyone needs it, it's jobstep.io, and don't say I didn't tell you, because people really are struggling like I was.
verdict.hook_en: 10 job offers? I got 10 job offers in the last week!
verdict.reason: It's the same story as N04: the creator shows an email inbox full of job offers as proof after months without work, then says the problem was the CV and shows how they fixed it with the tool.

Lo envías, esperas la respuesta y generalmente el problema está en el currículum. Lo mejor es que puede ayudarte de plataformas que hacen esto por ti en minutos. Por ejemplo esta guía me hizo preguntas sobre mi experiencia y ahí pude como detallarla de verdad, por ejemplo manejar de 3 a 4 cuentas de redes sociales en lugar de solamente gestión de cuentas y ahí envías tu currículum

Guys, I got a job, like I just got the confirmation, I've just been accepted.
That means two things: I've been unemployed for 4 months and I finally found something, so I'm going to have to go back to work.
That stings.
Mostly, I've been unemployed for 4 months, sending CVs left and right, and then I change one thing on my CV and I get accepted after a week.
The interview was so much fun, it went really well.
I think the main thing holding me back was my CV.
So what I did was go to this site, and it suggested I highlight results, which I never used to do.
So here, you see, this is my CV before it was optimized, like there are no results at all.
And here the AI kind of asks me: 'What were my results for each experience?'
So it guides me with questions and I answer them.
And here it suggests edits live, it's insane.
Like here, if I approve the change, boom, you see, it added it straight away.
And honestly, I think that's why I got a job.

verdict.english_script:
HR rejects all CVs like these.
I mean these really graphic, fancy ones.
So in 2026 you can't expect to find work with CVs like these.
A good CV should look like this: really boring and professional.
ATS filters go through the CVs, and ATS is a machine that weeds out the bad CVs.
My best friend works in HR, and she tipped me off about this really good site.
It's jobstep.io.
You just upload your CV there, it analyzes it, and right away you see a score and an assessment of your CV.
Here.
And if your score is under 50, your CV gets rejected automatically by the ATS filter.
Luckily you can improve it here, step by step.
We go through every step, and here you edit the layout, formatting, work experience and education.
At the end you can switch the template here, and I'm trying to pick the most minimalist one, so it fits really well.
